name_note: GTDB assigns this species to the genus Treponema_D, a split of the classical genus Treponema; sentences naming the genus Treponema therefore refer to a broader group than the GTDB genus.

sentences.text: Treponema peruense is a Gram-stain-negative, obligately anaerobic spirochaete isolated from a faecal sample from an individual residing in a remote Amazonian community in Peru.
Its closest relative by 16S rRNA gene sequence was the pig intestinal spirochaete Treponema succinifaciens, from which it was differentiated by alkaline phosphatase and alpha-glucosidase activities.

A study of faecal samples from hunter-gatherer and traditional agriculturalist communities in Peru and an urban-industrialized community reported that Treponema are characteristic of traditional gut microbiomes.
That study reported that these gut Treponema fall outside pathogenic clades, and suggested they are symbionts lost in urban-industrialized societies.
